name: Ravenna
title: Ravenna Ship Gauging | UTM for Offshore Vessels & Bulkers
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Ravenna for offshore supply vessels, bulk carriers, steel and chemical ships: ship repair yard and Candiano canal gauging.
h1: Thickness Gauging in Ravenna: Offshore Support, Bulk and Repair Quays
intro: Ravenna combines an inland canal port, an offshore energy support base and a ship repair industry on the northern Adriatic. Supply vessels, bulk carriers, steel and chemical ships work along the Candiano canal, and many ships are gauged here during repairs or cargo stops. Atlantis NDT sends thickness measurement technicians from India to the vessel, with no staff on the Romagna coast, and plans each job around the canal transit, the cargo window and the repair yard's programme.

highlights.p: Ravenna is a base for Adriatic gas fields and the engineering firms that serve them, so supply vessels and workboats need hull, tank and deck readings for class and charterer checks.

highlights.h: Ship repair yards on the canal
highlights.p: Repair yards along the Candiano canal handle dockings and steel renewal, so owners can combine a gauging programme with the yard stay and compare readings against the repair work list.
Bulk carriers with grain, fertiliser and raw materials, steel carriers and chemical ships call at the canal quays, bringing hold, hatch cover and tank gauging requests ahead of surveys.

port.h: The port of Ravenna: Porto Corsini, the Candiano canal and the inland quays
p: Ravenna is unusual among Adriatic ports because the city lies inland and the port reaches it by a long dredged channel, the Candiano canal. Ships enter from the sea at Porto Corsini between two moles, then travel along the canal to quays, terminals and yards on both banks, passing industrial areas where steelworks, chemical plants and bulk stores line the water. The channel is kept at a controlled depth by dredging and sets the maximum draught for ships heading inland. The tidal range is small, but the northern Adriatic produces storm surges and bora winds that can stop pilotage.

Cargo and service traffic are both substantial. Bulk carriers bring cereals, fertilisers, clays and other raw materials for local industry, and steel coil and plate move in and out on general cargo ships and multipurpose vessels. Chemical and product tankers serve the petrochemical sites, and ro-ro and container ships use dedicated terminals. Ravenna is also the centre of the Italian offshore industry on the Adriatic, so platform supply vessels, crane barges, pipelay support craft and other offshore ships are common, working from quays that have supported gas field projects for decades.

The ships that come to Ravenna are often there for a reason that suits gauging. Repair yards along the canal carry out dockings, hull blasting, steel renewal and conversions, and ships under repair provide excellent access to hull plating, tanks and decks. Bulk carriers spend days alongside discharging, which allows hold work. Offshore vessels return to base between contracts with a known idle period. Because the canal is long and transit takes time, ships tend to remain alongside rather than moving quickly, which gives the technicians a defined working window.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens in Ravenna: repair quays, canal berths and offshore bases
p: Ravenna has the strongest repair infrastructure of the northern Adriatic ports covered here. Yards on the canal handle dockings, steel renewal and refits, with floating docks and repair quays used by merchant and offshore ships, and a ship in the yard has hull plating exposed, tanks open and scaffolding in place. We can gauge at the start of the repair period to confirm the work list, during the job to check renewed steel, or at the end for the close-out file. The yard sets access rules, hot-work limits and permit procedures, and the superintendent arranges them with us in advance.

Away from the yards, canal berths suit cargo-stop gauging. Bulk carriers can be measured after discharge, steel carriers between loadings, and chemical ships at berths subject to terminal rules, which restrict entry to cargo tanks. Offshore supply vessels lie at quays used as support bases, where hulls, tanks and deck areas can be measured while the ship waits for a contract. Anchorage outside Porto Corsini is available for ships waiting for a berth, where an owner's condition check is possible when sea conditions allow.
list: Repair yards on the Candiano canal — hull plating, ballast tanks and deck structure gauged during docking, before, during or after steel renewal
Floating dock and repair quays — shell and bottom plating of coasters, offshore vessels and workboats once surfaces are cleaned
Bulk quays — hold frames, tank tops, hatch covers and coamings on cereal, fertiliser and raw material carriers after discharge
Steel and multipurpose quays — deck and hatch cover structure on steel carriers and general cargo ships between loading windows
Offshore support quays — hull, tank and deck gauging of supply vessels and workboats during idle periods between contracts
Anchorage off Porto Corsini — condition checks on ships waiting for a berth or laid up, by launch through the agent

context.h: Port state control and regulation for Ravenna's repair and offshore trades
p: Port state control in Ravenna is carried out by the Italian Coast Guard through the harbour master (Capitaneria di Porto), under the Paris MoU. Bulk carriers fall under ESP, and class surveyors decide what readings each survey needs, so a ship in a Ravenna yard often has the class surveyor and the gauging team working in the same tanks. Offshore vessels follow their class and flag requirements, and offshore charterers add their own vetting of structural condition, so a recent set of readings is a common request before a contract.

Wider rules shape demand as well. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials on ships calling at EU ports, and repair and conversion work in the yards is increasingly planned with the inventory in view. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime influence decisions about older ships, since reduced efficiency and rising running cost tilt the balance towards sale or recycling. In the offshore sector, projects for energy transition, such as carbon storage and wind support, bring new vessel types to the base, and owners entering that work want credible steel records.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Ravenna
jobs.p: Ravenna jobs are often tied to a repair yard stay or to the idle time of an offshore vessel. A ship in the yard offers broad access and a clear start and end date, so the gauging programme can be matched to the yard's work list. Ships at the quays offer shorter windows. The scope, permits, surface preparation and report format are agreed with the superintendent before the technicians travel from India, and open items are carried to the next stage of the repair.
list: Pre-docking gauging of a bulk carrier at a Ravenna quay, so the yard can quote steel renewal from measured readings
Hull, ballast tank and deck gauging of an offshore supply vessel in a repair yard before a new charter
Close-out readings on renewed plating at the end of a repair stay, to document the final condition for the class surveyor
Hold frame and hatch cover gauging on a grain or fertiliser carrier after discharge at the bulk quays
Condition survey of a workboat or crane barge at an offshore support quay ahead of sale or sub-charter

logistics: Bologna Guglielmo Marconi Airport is the usual entry point and is connected to Ravenna by road and rail, while Forli airport is closer but has fewer flights. The ship's agent, or the yard for ships under repair, arranges ISPS access and any permit needed for hot-work areas and docks. Our technicians are Indian nationals travelling on Schengen visas, so we begin the application when the job is confirmed and book flights once the yard slot or the quay date is firm. Yard stays allow more notice than cargo stops.

faqs.q: Can I combine gauging with a drydocking at a Ravenna yard?
faqs.a: Yes. We usually measure at the start of the stay, when the hull is blasted and tanks are open, so the work list is confirmed from readings. A second visit near the end checks renewed steel, and all results are combined in one file that the class surveyor and the owner can use.

faqs.q: Does the Candiano canal affect planning?
faqs.a: It affects the ship's movements rather than the gauging. Canal transit and pilotage take time, and storm surges or bora winds can stop movements, so arrival times can shift. We fix flights only when the quay or yard date is firm, and keep the scope prioritised in case the working window is shorter than planned.

faqs.q: Can you gauge offshore supply vessels between contracts?
faqs.a: Yes. Supply vessels and workboats often lie at the support quays for days or weeks between jobs, which allows a full programme on hull plating, ballast tanks and deck areas. Charterers often ask for recent readings before a new contract, and a report prepared in Ravenna answers that request.

faqs.q: Can chemical ship cargo tanks be gauged at the canal berths?
faqs.a: Not during cargo operations. Cargo tank entry needs a gas-free ship and a valid enclosed-space permit, which terminals do not allow while a ship is loading or discharging. At the berth we gauge deck, piping and ballast spaces, and plan cargo tank work for a yard stay.

faqs.q: How are surfaces prepared in a repair yard?
faqs.a: The yard usually blasts or cleans the hull, which gives ideal conditions for readings. We agree with the yard which areas are prepared and when, mark the measurement points on the drawings, and record the surface condition against each reading so that later comparisons are meaningful.
